newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN GERMAN LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN GERMAN LEAGUE.

text.p: Matches scheduled in the German league championship this weekend (last season's final standings in brackets, kick off times GMT): Playing Friday, kick of 1800 for both matches
VfB Stuttgart (4) v 1860 Munich (7)

Stuttgart, fourth last season and winners of the German Cup, will have a battle on their hands if they are to vie with star-studded Bayern Munich and Dortmund for the title. They nevertheless have a strong team with brilliant individual players such as Bulgarian playmaker Krasimir Balakov and international striker Fredi Bobic. They have lost Brazilian striker Giovane Elber, now with Bayern, and replaced him with Nigerian Jonathan Akpoborie, who joined from Hansa Rostock.
1860 Munich had a successful season, finishing seventh despite limited means. The team led by gifted Ghanaian Abdedi Pele aim at a top five finish.
Schalke (12) v Bayer Leverkusen (2)
An interesting clash between the surprise UEFA Cup winners and last season's league runners up, who gave Bayern Munich a hard time before settling for second place.

While shining on the European scene, Gelsenkirchen club Schalke were disappointing in the league, finishing a modest 12th. They have a new striker in Dutchman Rene Eijkelkamp, who joined from PSV Eindhoven.
Bayer Leverkusen have signed Brazilian midfielder Emerson from Gremio Porto Alegre. Playing Saturday, kick off 1330 for all five matches
Karlsruhe (6) v Werder Bremen (8)

Karslruhe lost two key-players in midfielders Michael Tarnat and Thorsten Fink, now with Bayern Munich. But they still look strong with gifted playmaker Thomas Haessler and South-African born striker Sean Dundee.

Werder Bremen, who had their moments of glory in the early 1990s by winning the Cup winners' Cup in 1992, the German title in 1993 and the German Cup the following year, made no spectacular signing during the close season.
Bochum (5) v Arminia Bielefeld (14)
Bochum, who finished a surprise fifth last season, signed Ukrainian striker Sergey Yuran from relegated Fortuna Duesseldorf.
Arminia Bielefeld, who narrowly avoided relegation, have no ambition other than to stay in the top league.
Cologne (10) v Duisburg (9)
Cologne, who disappointed by ending 10th in the 18-strong league, hope for better times after signing Rene Tretschok and Dennis Vogt from European champions Dortmund.
Duisburg finished their second season after being promoted from the second division in ninth position.
Hansa Rostock (15) v Wolfsburg (promoted)

Rostock, the town where Tour de France winner Jan Ullrich comes from, had a tough season and were happy to escape relegation. Croatian striker Igor Pamic has joined them from French second division Sochaux. They play Wolfsburg, promoted to the first division for the first time after finishing runners-up in last season's second division championship.
Bayern Munich (1) v Kaiserslautern (promoted)

Champions Bayern have replaced Juergen Klinsmann, now with Sampdoria, with Brazilian striker Giovane Elber, who joined from Stuttgart. They are favourites to retain the title but must beware of Kaiserslautern.

The 1991 champions spent only one season in the second division following their disastrous 1995-96 campaign. After winning the second division title, they are back with the best and trainer Otto Rehhagel believes they can fare well. Playing Sunday
Herta Berlin (promoted) v Borussia Dortmund (3) kick off

Herta Berlin are one of the attractions of the new season. The German champions in 1930 and 1931 are back in the first division with a new foreign star in Dutch international Brian Roy, who joined from Nottingham Forest.

They face Borussia Dortmund, who have made no major changes so far to the team who won the European Cup with a shock victory over Juventus in last May's final. They have a new coach in Italian Nevio Scala.
Hamburg (13) v Moenchengladbach (11) kick off 1600
Hamburg, the 1983 European champions, signed Polish international striker Jacek Dembinski from Widzew lodz after another disappointing season.
Moenchengladbach, who bought midfielder Marcel Witeczek from Bayern Munich, expect more from international playmaker Stefan Effenberg, far from his best form last season.
